chosen_property.label: performerIn
chosen_property.justification: The 'performerIn' schema.org property directly expresses a Person → Event relation and fits all instances.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess
candidates.comment: A biological function relation between a biochemical entity and the biological process it participates in. Also called participates in process, role in biological process, contributes to process. Examples: A protein is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'cell division'. An enzyme is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'metabolism'. A hormone is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'growth regulation'.

instances: Marvel Cinematic Universe -> 2026 San Diego Comic-Con announcement

chosen_property.label: organizer
chosen_property.justification: The 'organizer' schema.org property is in Event → Organization/Person; we use it in inverse direction.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: hostingOrganization
candidates.comment: A hosting organization relation between a member program or program membership and the organization that offers or manages it. Also called program provider, membership organization, host company. Examples: "A member program has a hosting organization 'Airline X'.", "The program membership is with a hosting organization.", "This program is hosted by a specific organization."

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: parentOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.

candidates.label: department
candidates.comment: An organizational structure relation between an organization and one of its departments. Also called: organizational unit, division, branch. Examples: "University" department "Computer Science Department", "Hospital" department "Emergency Room", "Retail Store" department "Pharmacy".

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

relations.definition: Attribution of a statement to a source.
relations.embedding_query_text: makes_claim: Attribution of a statement to a source.

instances: Kevin Feige -> Feige's comment on secrets and surprises

chosen_property.label: makesClaim
chosen_property.definition: A claim-making relation between a person and the statement they make.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses Person → Statement; a new property is needed.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: creditText
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a creative work and the text used to credit associated persons or organizations. Also called: attribution text, credit line, acknowledgment. Examples: "Movie" credit text "Directed by...", "Photograph" credit text "Photo by John Doe", "Research Paper" credit text "Funding provided by...". Distinct from creator, which identifies the primary author/creator.

candidates.label: creditedTo
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a music release and the group or artist it is credited to, if different from the primary artist. Also called: attributed to, release credit, presented by. Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: associatedMediaReview
candidates.comment: A media review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related media review, linked media assessment. Examples: "Review 'ClaimReview of Statement' associatedMediaReview 'MediaReview of Article'", "Review 'ProductReview' associatedMediaReview 'VideoReview'". Distinct from associatedClaimReview, which links to a claim review.

instances: Feige's comment on secrets and surprises -> 2026 San Diego Comic-Con announcement

chosen_property.label: isPartOfEvent
chosen_property.definition: A part-whole relation between a statement and the event it is part of.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses Statement → Event; a new property is needed.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: partOfInvoice
candidates.comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

chosen_property.label: organizer
chosen_property.justification: The 'organizer' schema.org property is in Event → Organization/Person; we use it in inverse direction.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
candidates.comment: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".

candidates.label: diseasePreventionInfo
candidates.comment: A disease prevention information relation between a special announcement and a URL or web content providing details about disease prevention. Also called "prevention guidelines", "health advice". Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: diseaseSpreadStatistics
candidates.comment: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".

candidates.label: schoolClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: Information regarding school closures, typically provided as a URL or web content within a special announcement. Also called school closing details, closure announcement, education disruption info. Examples: `Emergency Announcement` schoolClosuresInfo `URL to district website`, `Weather Alert` schoolClosuresInfo `Text about snow day`, `Public Health Notice` schoolClosuresInfo `WebContent on school status`.

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

relations.embedding_query_text: is_scheduled_for: Temporal planning of an event.

instances: Ryan Gosling joins MCU as Ghost Rider -> 2028

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: The 'startDate' schema.org property directly expresses Event → Date.

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: byMonthWeek
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the week(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "week of month", "monthly week recurrence", "on week of month". Examples: "Book club schedule byMonthWeek 2", "Team sync schedule byMonthWeek 1,3".

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: courseSchedule
candidates.comment: A temporal structure relation between a course instance and its length and pace. Also called: course timetable, class schedule, academic calendar. Examples: "Fall Semester Course" course schedule "Mondays and Wednesdays, 10:00-11:30 AM", "Intensive Workshop" course schedule "Full-day, 5 days", "Online Module" course schedule "Self-paced, complete within 8 weeks".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

relations.definition: Acting or embodying a character in a role.
relations.embedding_query_text: plays: Acting or embodying a character in a role.

instances: Ryan Gosling -> Ghost Rider
Nicolas Cage -> Ghost Rider

chosen_property.label: playsCharacter
chosen_property.definition: A relation between a person and the fictional character they portray.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses Person → Person for character portrayal; a new property is needed.

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: actors
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

chosen_property.label: originatedIn
chosen_property.definition: A relation between a character and the publication event where they first appeared.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses Person → PublicationEvent for character origin; a new property is needed.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: artist
candidates.comment: A person who is the primary creator of a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork, especially in non-line art mediums. Also called: creator, illustrator, visual creator. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Starry Night' artist 'Vincent van Gogh'", "ComicIssue 'Issue #1' artist 'Frank Miller'", "ComicStory 'Origin Story' artist 'Alex Ross'". Distinct from author, which is a more general term for the creator of content, often textual.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: firstPerformance

chosen_property.label: partnerOf
chosen_property.definition: A relation between two people in a romantic relationship.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses Person → Person for romantic partners; a new property is needed.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: colleague
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and another person who is their colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John colleague Jane", "Professor Smith colleague 'https://example.com/prof-jones'". Distinct from colleagues, which is a plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: pronouns
candidates.comment: A pronoun relation between a person and the linguistic terms they use to refer to themselves. Also called preferred pronouns, self-identification pronouns. Examples: "A person uses pronouns 'she/her'.", "Another person uses pronouns 'they/them'.", "A third person uses pronouns 'he/him'."

candidates.label: parent
candidates.comment: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor. Examples: "Child A parent 'Parent B'", "Person X parent 'Mother Y'", "Person Z parent 'Father W'". Distinct from children, which describes the offspring.

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their child. Also called "offspring", "son", "daughter". Examples: "John children Jane", "Mary children Peter". Distinct from parent, which indicates the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: colleagues
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and other persons who are their colleagues. Also called "co-workers", "associates", "professional peers". Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."
